summary: Candidate A is materially closer to the frozen contract and keeps the change localized. It still needs correction before merge, but Candidate B explicitly broadens retry behavior across RawClient and duplicates Files.Add machinery, both directly contrary to the contract.
reasons: A reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile with the required field name and exposes the exact Upload signature.
A’s Upload retry test uses an actual *os.File source and verifies filename and content on every attempt, providing stronger streamed-content replay coverage than B’s Upload retry test.
A factors request construction, options, decoding, and error handling into one shared path; B copies the Files.Add implementation into Upload instead of routing through Add.

B changes RawClient.Do for every io.Reader request and advertises changed Files.Update behavior, despite the explicit prohibition on refactoring unrelated retry machinery or changing Update semantics/options behavior indirectly through global buffering effects.
risks_a: A changes FilesService.Add by eagerly buffering every body, violating the requirement to preserve its existing behavior and potentially changing memory use, read timing, and no-retry streaming semantics.
Upload calls the new private add helper rather than the existing public Add method, so it does not literally satisfy the required routing contract.
The visible tests do not cover empty-filename validation, nil content, or Upload source-reader failures; the combined validation error is also less precise.
risks_b: The global RawClient buffering mechanism is an out-of-scope retry refactor and affects all reader-bodied requests, including Files.Update.
Upload duplicates Add’s option handling, request construction, decoding, and missing-data error logic, creating maintenance drift and violating the required reuse path.

Its Upload retry test only discards request bodies and does not verify that multipart filename and content survive the retry; the stronger replay assertions are attached to the out-of-scope global Add behavior instead.
